$comment: Every IPC channel main serves while the vault is locked: CHANNEL_POLICY rows other than unlocked, send and event (src/main/ipcGuard.ts). tools/guards/ipcChannels.test.ts requires this list to equal the table; the ratchet refuses an addition, so a new one needs the maintainer.
pre-unlock:openExternal: Links on the lock screen (help, recovery instructions); https and mailto only through openExternalSafe.
pre-unlock:updateState: The lock screen shows that an update is ready; read-only state.
pre-unlock:chromeMenu: The custom title bar draws the application menu on the lock screen.
pre-unlock:appVersion: The lock screen shows the version; public.
pre-unlock:vaultStatus: The lock screen needs the vault state to know what to ask for.
pre-unlock:vaultUnlock: Unlocking with the password is what the lock screen is for.
pre-unlock:vaultQuickUnlock: Unlocking with the OS keychain (Touch ID or the login keyring).
flush:docsAppend: The renderer's last edit lands during the lock's flush step, while the state is already locking (§6.4).
flush:blobsPut: An image pasted just before the lock lands during the flush step (§6.4).
send-pre-unlock:themesInitial: The lock screen window reads its theme synchronously at start.
send-pre-unlock:chromeKind: The lock screen window asks which title bar to draw.
send-pre-unlock:chromeSetColors: The lock screen sets its title bar colours.
send-pre-unlock:chromeToggleMaximize: Double-clicking the lock screen's title bar.
send-pre-unlock:chromeInvokeMenu: Clicking an item of the lock screen's custom title-bar menu, the same menu the native bar shows.
send-pre-unlock:vaultFlushed: The renderer's reply to the flush request, sent while the state is locking.
send-pre-unlock:vaultLock: Locking needs no permission: the worst a page can do with it is lock the vault.
